items.title: A unique factorization domain is integrally closed in its fraction field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a unique factorization domain is normal, that is, integrally closed in its fraction field (statement lines 29817-29820). The proof does not use the theory of Dedekind domains or a minimal polynomial: it writes an integral element as a unit times a product of powers of pairwise non-associate irreducibles with integer exponents, assumes one exponent is negative, and raises the integrality equation into an identity that exhibits a product of primes as divisible by the offending irreducible, contradicting uniqueness of factorization (proof lines 29822-29836). The choice of exponent N to clear denominators is the substance, and the author writes the resulting identity out. H2.
